products.name: Atlas Leather Pouf
products.blurb: Hand-stitched sheep leather, henna-dyed in small batches. Ships flat — you fill it at home.
products.description: Hand-stitched in a small workshop in the Marrakech medina by master leather artisan Mohammed Tazi. Naturally tanned sheep leather, henna-dyed in small batches. Ships flat — you fill it with old clothes, blankets, or polyester stuffing (about 12–15 kg).

details.title: Materials & care
list: 100% natural sheep leather, tanned without chromium
Henna and indigo natural dyes — colors may vary slightly
Wipe clean with a damp cloth · do not soak
Apply natural leather conditioner every 6 months

details.title: How to stuff your pouf
details.text: Your pouf ships unstuffed to keep shipping affordable. Fill it through the bottom zipper with old t-shirts, towels, blankets, or about 12–15 kg of polyester filling. It takes about 15 minutes — fill firmly so it holds its shape.

details.title: The artisan’s story
details.text: Mohammed Tazi has worked leather in the Marrakech medina for 27 years. His workshop near the Bahia Palace produces around 8 poufs per week, each entirely by hand. We pay him 3× the local market rate and source his leather from a small tannery in Fes.

artisan.name: Mohammed Tazi
artisan.bio1: Mohammed’s small workshop sits in a forgotten alley behind the Bahia Palace. He works alone, six days a week, producing around eight poufs and a handful of bags. We met him in 2024 and he became our first leather partner.
artisan.bio2: Every piece you order is made specifically for you — no warehouse, no overstock. Your pouf will leave his hands within 5–7 days of your order.

products.name: Pierced Brass Lantern
products.blurb: Hand-pierced in the Fes medina, casting filigree shadows across the room when lit.
products.description: Hand-pierced brass lantern from the metalworkers of the Fes medina, using techniques unchanged since the Marinid era. Each one throws intricate filigree shadows across walls and ceiling when lit. Fits a standard tea light or small LED candle.

products.name: Handmade Babouches
products.blurb: Soft hand-stitched leather slippers, dyed with saffron and pomegranate.
products.description: Traditional Moroccan babouches, hand-stitched from supple goat leather and dyed with saffron and pomegranate skin. Worn indoors and out for centuries across the Maghreb. Unisex sizing — they soften and mould to your foot within days.

products.name: Glazed Cooking Tagine
products.blurb: A real cooking tagine from Safi, Morocco’s pottery capital — not a decorative one.
products.description: A true cooking tagine — not a decorative piece — thrown and glazed by potters in Safi, Morocco’s ceramic capital. The conical lid circulates steam to slow-cook meat and vegetables with almost no water. Season it before first use; safe on a diffuser over flame or in the oven.

products.name: Woven Souk Basket
products.blurb: Hand-woven palm-leaf basket with stitched leather handles. Market bag or home storage.
products.description: Hand-woven from doum palm leaf by weavers in Salé, finished with hand-stitched leather handles. Equally at home as a market bag, a beach tote, or storage for blankets and toys. Each one is unique in weave and tone.

products.name: Beni Ourain Berber Rug
products.blurb: Undyed wool, hand-knotted over 30–90 days by women of the Aït Bouguemez valley.
products.description: A genuine Beni Ourain rug, hand-knotted from undyed Atlas sheep wool by women of the Aït Bouguemez valley. The diamond and line motifs are personal — woven from memory, never copied. Each rug takes between 30 and 90 days. No two are alike, and once one is gone it cannot be remade.

artisan.name: Fatima Z.
artisan.bio1: Fatima has been weaving Beni Ourain rugs since she was seven, taught by her grandmother high in the Atlas. Each rug takes between 30 and 90 days — a single mistake means starting over.
artisan.bio2: She works within a women’s cooperative that we pay directly, with no middlemen between her loom and your floor.

products.name: Pure Argan Oil
products.blurb: Cold-pressed cosmetic argan oil from a women’s cooperative near Essaouira.
products.description: Cold-pressed cosmetic-grade argan oil from a women’s cooperative near Essaouira, where the argan tree grows nowhere else on earth. Unroasted and unscented, for skin, hair and nails. 50 ml amber glass bottle with dropper.

products.name: Hand-Embroidered Cushion
products.blurb: Cotton cushion cover with fassi-style hand embroidery from the blue city.
products.description: A cotton cushion cover hand-embroidered in the fassi tradition by artisans in blue-walled Chefchaouen. Hidden zip, 45 × 45 cm, cover only. Each takes two to three days of needlework.

products.name: Hand-Stitched Leather Tote
products.blurb: Roomy full-grain leather tote, saddle-stitched by hand in the medina.
products.description: A roomy, unlined full-grain leather tote, saddle-stitched entirely by hand in the Marrakech medina. It starts firm and develops a deep patina with use. Fits a 13" laptop, a market haul, or a weekend away.

products.name: Damask Rose Water
products.blurb: Steam-distilled from Damask roses in the Valley of Roses. A toner and a ritual.
products.description: Steam-distilled from Damask roses harvested at dawn in the Valley of Roses (Kelaat M’Gouna). A gentle facial toner and a centuries-old ritual mist. Nothing added — just rose and water. 100 ml glass bottle.

products.name: Beldi Black Soap
products.blurb: The olive-based hammam soap, traditionally paired with a kessa exfoliating glove.
products.description: Beldi black soap — the soft, olive-based paste at the heart of the Moroccan hammam ritual. Massage on, leave a few minutes, then scrub with the included kessa glove. Leaves skin remarkably smooth. 200 g jar.

products.name: Azilal Berber Rug
products.blurb: A wilder cousin of the Beni Ourain — abstract, colourful, full of story.
products.description: Azilal rugs are the wilder, more colourful cousins of the Beni Ourain — woven on a natural wool ground with bursts of dyed thread arranged from imagination, not pattern. Each is a one-of-a-kind diary of its weaver. Roughly 1.5 × 2.5 m.

products.name: Handira Wedding Blanket
products.blurb: A sequined Amazigh wedding blanket (handira), hand-woven by women of the Middle Atlas.
products.description: The handira is woven by Amazigh women for a bride to wear at her wedding, then kept for life as a blanket and heirloom. Hand-woven wool studded with hundreds of small metal sequins — believed to catch the light and ward off the evil eye. Every piece is unique. Roughly 1.3 × 2 m.
